slides.say: Yoav claims: there are more three-digit numbers divisible by both three and five, than three-digit numbers divisible by seventeen. Michal claims: there are more three-digit numbers divisible by both three and seven, than three-digit numbers divisible by both two and thirteen. Which of the following is correct?

So two claims about how many numbers divide by something. And remember, divisible by both three and five means divisible by fifteen, because three and five share no factor. In the same way, three and seven make twenty-one, and two and thirteen make twenty-six. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, counting the multiples, and then comparing without counting.

[short pause] Let's start by counting. The three-digit numbers go from a hundred to nine hundred ninety-nine. Fifteen times six is ninety, still two digits, so the first one is fifteen times seven, a hundred five.

And the last? Fifteen times sixty is nine hundred, and fifteen times six is ninety, so fifteen times sixty-six is nine hundred ninety. One more fifteen is a thousand five, too big. So the multiples go from fifteen times seven to fifteen times sixty-six.

How many is that? Sixty-six minus seven, plus one. Why plus one? Both ends count. From three to seven there are five numbers, three, four, five, six, seven, and seven minus three is only four. So sixty-six minus seven is fifty-nine, and plus one is sixty.

Seventeen. Seventeen times six is a hundred two, the first three-digit one. And seventeen times sixty is a thousand twenty, minus two seventeens, thirty-four, so seventeen times fifty-eight is nine hundred eighty-six. Fifty-eight minus six is fifty-two, and plus one is fifty-three. Sixty is more than fifty-three, so Yoav is right.
Michal. Twenty-one times five is a hundred five, and twenty-one times forty-seven is nine hundred eighty-seven. Forty-seven minus five is forty-two, and plus one is forty-three.

Twenty-six times four is a hundred four, and twenty-six times thirty-eight is nine hundred eighty-eight. Thirty-eight minus four is thirty-four, and plus one is thirty-five. Forty-three is more than thirty-five, so Michal is right too. Both are right, choice number three.

[pause] Another way, without counting at all. Every fifteenth number divides by fifteen, and every seventeenth divides by seventeen. One in every fifteen is more than one in every seventeen. So fifteen has more multiples, and Yoav is right.
The same for Michal. One in every twenty-one is more than one in every twenty-six. So the smaller the divisor, the more multiples it has, and both are right.
Why can we trust it here? The range is long, nine hundred numbers, so the difference is big. In a short range, count exactly. Choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
